title: Digital expansion is intensifying demand for energy, water, minerals, and devices while distributing ecological costs unevenly
source_unit: UNCTAD, Digital Economy Report 2024: Shaping an environmentally sustainable and inclusive digital future
geography: Global digital economy, ICT devices and infrastructure, digital trade, critical-mineral supply chains, and developing-country ecological and economic exposure

denominator.unit: global digital-economy and ICT infrastructure frame

business_ecommerce_2022.unit: US dollars in business e-commerce sales in 2022 across 43 countries, approximately

digital_electricity_share.unit: percent estimated share of global electricity use from digital devices, data centres, and ICT networks

observations.method: UNCTAD synthesis of device shipments, e-commerce statistics, ICT infrastructure, energy-use estimates, and digitalization life-cycle analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Digital-footprint estimates vary with system boundaries, device lifetimes, electricity mixes, indirect effects, and data availability; projections are scenario-dependent.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, firms, data-centre operators, ICT networks, e-commerce markets, device workers, connected and unconnected populations, and places hosting digital infrastructure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital services can reduce some travel, material, or transaction costs and improve access, but rebound effects, device turnover, and infrastructure growth can offset efficiency gains.

denominator.unit: global data-centre and digital-infrastructure resource-use frame

data_centres_energy_2022.unit: terawatt-hours of estimated data-centre electricity consumption globally in 2022

data_centres_energy_2026.unit: terawatt-hours of projected data-centre electricity consumption globally in 2026

google_water_2022.unit: cubic metres of water consumed by Google data centres and offices in 2022, approximately

water_stress_exposure.unit: percent of direct data-centre server water footprint in the United States reportedly sourced from moderately to highly water-stressed watersheds

observations.method: UNCTAD compilation of data-centre energy and water estimates, company disclosures, and location-specific water-stress analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Energy and water footprints depend on accounting boundaries, cooling technology, grid mix, siting, climate, and company disclosure; global projections are not local service-incidence estimates.
observations.subgroup: Data-centre host communities, electricity and water utilities, households sharing local infrastructure, technology firms, regulators, and water-stressed regions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved efficiency, low-carbon power, water recycling, alternative cooling, and careful siting can reduce local and global impacts; digital infrastructure is not uniformly harmful.

denominator.unit: global critical-mineral, digital-waste, and circularity frame

critical_mineral_demand_change.unit: percent projected increase by 2050 in demand for cobalt, graphite, and lithium cited by the report

cobalt_production_concentration.unit: percent of global cobalt production from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2023

lithium_production_concentration.unit: percent of global lithium production from Australia and Chile in 2023

developing_country_e_waste_collection.unit: percent of digital waste formally collected in developing countries in 2022

developed_country_e_waste_collection.unit: percent of digital waste formally collected in developed countries in 2022

global_circularity.unit: percent estimated share of the global economy considered circular

observations.method: UNCTAD analysis of critical-mineral supply concentration, digital-waste flows, formal collection, value-chain position, and circular-economy indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Mineral concentration and waste statistics use different years, definitions, and reporting systems; projected demand is sensitive to technology, substitution, recycling, and policy assumptions.
observations.subgroup: Mineral-rich developing countries, mining and processing communities, device consumers, informal waste workers, recyclers, farmers and households competing for water, and downstream technology firms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mineral demand can create value-chain and employment opportunities when countries add value and protect rights; formal collection and repair can improve recovery, jobs, and material efficiency.

related_sources.claim: UNCTAD report launch and environmental-footprint framing.
UNCTAD summary of unequal digital ecological burdens and circularity recommendations.

boundary: This record adds a digital-consumption-to-energy, water, minerals, e-waste, value-chain, and geopolitical-resource route. It is not household device-use data, local environmental-impact measurement, individual consumer behavior, or proof of causal effects from digitalization on communities.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNCTAD Digital Economy Report publication page, full report, overview, launch page, and press material were retrieved; device, e-commerce, electricity, data-centre, water, mineral, e-waste, and circularity claims were cross-checked.
